title: .respawnpack/runtime/rollover/<host>-<conversationId>/<subjectId>.consumed.json — the exactly-once claim receipt
description: Written by core/lifecycle/consumable.js's consume() with `wx` (O_EXCL / CREATE_NEW): exactly one caller across any number of processes creates this file, and every other caller learns it already existed. Generic on purpose — the ROLLOVER HANDOFF is the first and, in W2, the only subject that claims through it (core/state/handoff.js's own consume() delegates here), but the mechanism and this schema are not handoff-specific: `subjectId` names whatever was claimed. GITIGNORED, machine-local. No schemaVersion: a receipt this small, with a lifetime bound to one subjectId and never rewritten once created, carries no format a future reader needs to distinguish from an earlier one.

note.description: A human-readable reason the caller supplied. Null is legal — not every consumer names one.

extra.description: Caller-defined payload, present only when the caller supplied one. The rollover handoff's own consumption records {verifiedDigest, contextCycleId, exactNextAction} here — see core/state/handoff.js consume(). Deliberately unconstrained beyond its own type: this primitive is reused by whatever else needs exactly-once consumption, and a schema that named one caller's fields would be documenting a caller, not the primitive.
